A1R.title: The queen used to be the weakest piece in chess #shorts
A1R.desc:
For centuries the queen could only move one square diagonally. Around 1475 in Valencia, Spain, she got the moves of a rook and a bishop combined, and games got so much faster that people called it mad queen chess. The oldest surviving game with the new queen comes from a Valencian poem, Scachs d'amor, and the queen gives the mate herself.

What rule would you change in chess?

#chess #chesshistory #chessfacts

GENP.title: This looks like cheating, but it's a real chess move #shorts
GENP.desc:
En passant: when a pawn moves two squares and lands next to an enemy pawn, that pawn can take it as if it had moved only one square, but only on the very next move. The rule dates from the 15th century, when pawns got their two-square first move.

Did you know this rule?

#chess #enpassant #chessrules
